title: Shaky Picks (awwwards Honorable Mention, Jul 2026)
take: A full ring of about 30 small cards circles one centred title and Start button, spun by trig with GSAP states: swap the title for the 3D crown and the tiles for real card art.

title: Rabo Art Collection (awwwards Honorable Mention, Sep 2025)
take: Hundreds of artworks on a tilted 3D ellipse that passes in front of and behind the centre title: take that depth ordering so near cards cross over the crown and far ones go behind it. (Live site refused the headless browser; image is the awwwards submission shot.)

title: 3D Orbit Gallery (21st.dev component)
take: Ready React/WebGL ring of image planes on black with an empty centre: closest copy-prompt starting point; drop the crown into the middle and restyle to navy.

title: ChronosEngine (21st.dev component)
take: A glowing gold core with shards orbiting at different radii on a navy grid: already in the Crowns palette; take the multi-radius orbit and the core glow, with cards in place of shards.

title: Unveil studio site
take: Image planes stacked in real 3D perspective, fading into depth (the model the Clauder hub carousel was built from): take the camera angle and plane spacing, not the white page.

title: Punchi-Kun interactive hero (Dribbble)
take: The 3D object stays fixed in the centre while a curved arc of picks rotates beneath it with a 2 / 5 counter and arrows: a calmer, navigable version of the orbit.

title: DepthForge 3D slider (Dribbble)
take: One 3D object with a tilted orbital ring around it, framed by a heavy condensed headline on the left: shows how the centrepiece and Anton-style type share a hero.

title: Spinning 3D card ring (P's DRD, Pinterest video)
take: From DRD: 8 to 10 cards on a ring tilted about 20 degrees, linear 360 degrees per about 12 s, back arc blurred and greyed so the front cards pop. Take the motion recipe, ignore the chart cards.

title: Interactive 3D Photo Carousel, GSAP and CSS (Dribbble)
take: Cards bow round the viewer in a shallow arc with the front card named underneath: nearest to today's Crowns carousel, useful as the no-crown fallback.

title: James Murray 3D portfolio (awwwards, Jan 2026)
take: A central globe with project tiles orbiting at different depths, click a tile to enter: proof that object plus orbiting items works as navigation. Leave the sci-fi blue styling.

title: Scryfall set page: Final Fantasy (FIN)
take: One slim set header (icon, 598 cards, release date, total set value in USD, EUR and TIX) with Jump to / Images / sorted by controls, then a dense card-image grid: the fastest whole-set browse found.

title: Player Album team page (awwwards Honorable Mention, Jun 2026)
take: One page per team: crest as the centrepiece, owned stickers shown, missing ones as blank slots, 0/11 counter in the header: turns have vs need into an album.

title: Magic: The Hobbit Card Image Gallery (official)
take: Set hero with key art, title and release date, a Where to Buy strip, then cards grouped by colour with counts (White 83) plus filters and search: set hero and grouped browse in one page.

title: Pokedesk card collector app (Dribbble)
take: Set row with the real Brilliant Stars logo, a completion bar (25%, 3 of 230 cards) and total value, then owned cards with prices: the collector framing a tracker set page needs.

title: GoShuin stamp journal (awwwards, Oct 2026)
take: A collection presented as a paged book: title and tagline on the left page, art on the right, page counter along the bottom: premium album pacing instead of a grid.

title: Qatar Museums Online Collection (awwwards, Jan 2026)
take: Search bar and category chips float over a loose wall of cut-out objects on white: browsing feels like a vitrine, not a table.

title: Karma Worlds archive (awwwards, Oct 2026)
take: Every track drawn as its own card and laid out in themed worlds: a whole archive as one explorable field with per-item art.

title: One Piece Card Game card list (official)
take: Booster selector, colour / card type / illustration / block filters, then a 169-result card grid: the filter vocabulary collectors already know.

title: PIKADEX Pokemon card store and collection (Dribbble)
take: Mobile concept pairing a spotlight card and an owned-card grid with prices: a reference for the phone version of the set page.

title: TCGplayer Prismatic Evolutions price guide
take: The functional baseline: every card as a sortable row (printing, condition, rarity, number, market price, add to cart). Match its speed, not its look.

title: Nothing Phone (3) product page
take: Product image centred with feature callouts floating round it as small tiles, and a compact buy panel (colour, storage, price, add to bag, pick up today) docked over the image: the most distinctive PDP found.

title: StockX: Chaos Rising Pokemon Center Elite Trainer Box
take: The exact sealed product Crowns tracks: Buy Now price beside Make Offer, last sale and highest offer, delivery date, then Buyer Promise and StockX Verified rows. Trust details for sealed product.

title: Alt graded card listing (Rayquaza VMAX, PSA 10)
take: Slab photo, PSA grade and population, list price with Buy Now / Offer, and a one-year Alt Value chart with range tabs: the data-backed trust a single-card page needs.

title: Teenage Engineering EP-133 store page
take: Large product image left; name, price, ships from the U.S. and one black add to cart on the right; specs as a plain list. Extreme restraint.

title: Apple: Shop iPhone 18 Pro
take: Model choice as stacked selectable cards with price and monthly next to a large image: the configure-then-buy step pattern.

title: Analogue 3D launch page
take: The console on black with its own cartridges floating round it under one big headline: sells the object before the buy flow (and is itself a centrepiece with orbit).

title: Playdate shop (out of stock state)
take: Honest sold-out state: Out of stock pill, a notify-me form at the top, product still fully presented with price: a template for a sold-out booster box.

title: Off-White luxury PDP (Dribbble)
take: Vertical thumbnail rail, one big image, size grid, add to bag beside buy now, accordions for details and shipping: the luxury fashion PDP skeleton.

title: Chronoswiss tourbillon watch store (Dribbble)
take: Dark watch hero with the piece centred, model name stacked left and a strip of story images below: luxury pacing for a single collectible.

title: Skeltec watch store, dark (Dribbble)
take: Near-black stage, product lit from one side, a single copper accent on the buy control: one-accent discipline for a dark store.

title: Pokemon TCG Pocket (App Store screenshots)
take: The reference interaction: pick a pack, swipe across the top and the tear follows your finger, then the cards. First screenshot shows the pack screen; copy the gesture, not the pastel UI.

title: Pack Opening 3D, official sports cards (Dribbble)
take: Gold foil pack with real crinkle and specular highlights on near-black: the material quality a 3D pack must hit, and already gold on dark like Crowns.

title: FrameMon pack opener (Framer community entry)
take: Browser pack opener (Open a pack. Pull a card.) on dark navy; per the entry you drag along the seam and the lid curls away: proof the tear works on the web, not just in an app.

title: Player Album scratch reveal (awwwards Honorable Mention, Jun 2026)
take: Scratch-to-reveal on each sticker slot: the player appears under your cursor stroke by stroke. Same earn-the-reveal feeling as a tear, in plain web.

title: 3D Pack Opening interactive app concept (Dribbble)
take: Pack fills the screen in fire-lit foil just before the tear: the dramatic light for the moment of anticipation.

title: Card Pack Opening Animation (Dribbble)
take: Booster with crimped ends, a holo art window and a brand header on dark: a clean model of real pack geometry to build in 3D.

title: Cardshop app pack opening (Dribbble)
take: Black pack backed by a burst of coloured light: a rarity glow that hints at what is inside before the tear.

title: Pack Opening Animation, Core Pack (Dribbble)
take: A single tilted pack in soft grey studio light: the restrained version that would sit quietly on Crowns navy.

title: Just The Rip (Threshline portfolio)
take: A real platform that rips real packs online and ships the physical cards: a business-model reference more than a look.

title: Ruler Picker, night (21st.dev component)
take: Big number readout (72.4) above a tick ruler that you drag; it coasts and settles, with keyboard and wheel support: almost exactly the bottom dial wanted, ready as a copy-prompt.

title: Dorot: The Jewish Timeline (awwwards, Jul 2026)
take: Range readout pinned at both ends (580 / 1010) over lanes of dots, plus a mini-map strip along the bottom to jump anywhere: a long horizontal set where you always know where you are.

title: OSI 90th anniversary timeline (awwwards Honorable Mention, Jul 2026)
take: Years laid on a shallow arc like a dial; the current year sits at top centre and the rest curve away: a dial, not a bar.

title: 18 Years of Buro (awwwards Site of the Day, Sep 2025)
take: Years plotted on a spiral of ellipses with the first and last year pinned in the corners (2006 / 2024): a scrubber that doubles as the hero graphic.

title: Filmstrip Scrub (21st.dev component)
take: Strip of thumbnails with a spring-loaded playhead and a live monospace timecode; drag or hover the strip to crossfade the big preview above.

title: Timeline Scrubber, dark (Dribbble)
take: Three hairline scrubber variants on black with ticks, a labelled playhead and range handles: no chrome, only lines and one label.

title: Precision Scrubber (Dribbble)
take: Drag the timecode label itself to scrub, swipe moves one frame at a time, thumbnails ride above: annotated interaction rules worth copying.

title: Traversing Days in a Timeline (Dribbble)
take: A card stack driven by a scrubber along the bottom: scrubbing swaps the big card above, which is the set page browse pattern.

title: Timeline with ticks and NOW marker (Dribbble)
take: Ticked strip with dated labels, coloured event marks and a red NOW marker: the simplest readable version (small, older shot).

title: PokeData home
take: On dark: the real 30th Celebration set logo, set name, release date and All cards link, then a row of that set's top cards with prices. Exactly the feature-then-row pattern with a real set mark.

title: Netflix Trending Now
take: Ranked row with huge outlined numerals 1 to 10 tucked behind each poster: rank reads before the art. Could rank the hottest sets or cards.

title: Collectr site (competitor)
take: A two-column grid of real game logos on dark tiles (Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Flesh and Blood, Dragon Ball Fusion World, Weiss Schwarz, Star Wars Unlimited) beside the portfolio phone: how mixed TCG marks sit together.

title: Magic: Latest Products (official)
take: Four tall key-art panels side by side, each with set name and release month at the foot: a cinematic new-releases strip.

title: Fanatics Collect home
take: Feature tiles of graded slabs per weekly auction, then a Trending searches chip row (Charizard, Gengar, Riftbound and more): feature, then what is hot.

title: Alt home: Featured Auctions
take: Row of slab photos with current bid and time left on dark, Top rising / falling tabs by category below: a market-moving strip.

title: GOAT home: Just Dropped
take: Dense black grid of cut-out sneakers with an item count, then New in collab rows: drops as a calm product wall, no banners.

title: Pokellector home
take: Newest TCG series shown as a row of real set logos, then the latest set's cards: dated look, right content model.

title: TCG Collector home
take: Set chips made of a real set logo plus a completion bar (69%): new-set strip and your-progress in one tile.

title: TCGplayer home
take: Full-width banner for the newest set, then a Best Sellers product row: the marketplace default to beat.
